answer: One concrete defence is to require every new agent to enter through a single audited inlet and prove a costly, checkable history before it can trade. The agent stakes a small deposit, links a public record of completed work, and must collect endorsements from two independent, long-lived registries, cedar and juniper, which verify different evidence and never share the same operators. A flood of fake identities then fails because each fake must pay, build history, and pass both independent checks, while a genuine newcomer passes once and reuses that proof across the market.
